title: NyxAI Q4 health pulse and roadmap sync
summary: Quarterly health pulse: review of usage trends, an unexpected cost spike in October, two brief latency incidents, and a roadmap alignment for a Dedicated pilot. Agreed next steps include a cost breakdown spreadsheet, a private deployment feasibility doc, and a short perf benchmark run in staging.
next_steps: Redwood to send cost breakdown by model variant and date range (Alex)
Customer to provide list of top 5 production prompts for eval (Sofia)
Share Private deployment checklist and SAML guide (Miguel)
action_items: Alex Kim - send October cost CSV and per-model token counts - due 2027-11-08
Sofia Patel - share top 5 prompts + expected QPS pattern - due 2027-11-10
Priya Nair & Ethan Zhang - agree pilot window and target latency SLOs - due 2027-11-12

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-11-03 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Miguel (Redwood CSM), Sofia (NyxAI Head of ML), Ethan (NyxAI Cloud), Laura (NyxAI CTO), Ravi (NyxAI SRE)

Auto-summary (auto): Quarterly health pulse; cost spike review; Dedicated pilot ask; security checklist request.

[00:00] Alex: all right everyone thanks for joining, um this is the nyxai q4 health pulse, i think we have about 50 minutes, we'll try to keep it tight. miguel can you do a 1-min context?
[00:10] Miguel: yeah quick context, last quarter we saw steady adoption, october had an anomalous cost increase — we flagged on the invoice, we spun up a quick root cause and there were two short latency incidents in us-west-2, otherwise adoption looks good.
[00:26] Sofia: thanks, yes from our side october's spike hit our finance alarms, and we need the breakdown because the execs asked for model-level attribution. also want to talk about the dedicated pilot timeline.
[00:38] Priya: ok quick agenda — usage & cost, reliability incidents, pilot scoping, security items. sound good?
[00:44] Laura: yep that's fine.

[02:05] Alex: starting with usage — since sept we've seen 18% month-over-month growth in tokens, but the oddity is a 3-day tail where average sequence length doubled for a few customers, likely a training job or very long chat sessions. the billing shows a jump in 2027-10-12 to 10-14 window.
[02:28] Ethan: on our side we had one microservice that fell back to a debug mode and started sending longer contexts, that was fixed on the 14th, so that aligns. i can share the pod logs.
[02:42] Sofia: yeah that seems like it. can you also confirm which model variants were in use — quantized vs full precision?
[02:48] Priya: quick note — Redwood's routing will fall back to the full fp32 variant if a quantized cache miss happens, and that can spike cost. i'll pull the model variant usage by date.

[04:10] Ravi: a question on caching — we saw references to k v cache, sometimes the transcript reads "K V cash" which made us laugh, but how does Redwood's prefix caching behave with multi-tenant sessions?
[04:23] Priya: good one — in hosted we do prefix/KV cache per customer-session; for Dedicated we can pin caches to the pool which reduces cross-tenant misses. if you have long-lived sessions it's definitely worth Dedicated or Private to keep cache warm.

[06:00] Alex: moving to the incidents — two short tail-latency spikes (6–8s p50 -> p95) during 10/14 and 10/20 in us-west-2. latency didn't breach the SLA but caused client retries. we traced to a scheduling queuing edge when autoscale was triggered.
[06:21] Ethan: on our side we saw the retries amplify traffic and then it cascaded; we adjusted client retry jitter which mitigated. question: are there rate limit configs that would prevent the cascade?
[06:32] Miguel: yes, there's per-token and per-route soft limits; we can show suggested settings. also recommend client-side exponential backoff with jitter.

[08:15] Sofia: security — our security team asked about SSO and SAML, plus KMS integration for private keys, and audit logs retention beyond 90 days. can redwood support 365-day audit logs for Dedicated/Private?
[08:30] Miguel: Dedicated and Private both support extended audit retention as an add-on; for Hosted we have a 90-day default. for KMS, Private supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations, we'll share the checklist.

[10:05] Alex: ok pilot ask — nyxai is considering a 3-month Dedicated pilot to hit consistent p95 < 500ms on their inference path and reduce token costs by 20% via quantization and prefix caching. priya, can you run through what we'd need to scope?
[10:20] Priya: sure, scope includes baseline perf run, model variant selection (quantized profiles), expected QPS, sequence length distribution, and rollout policy (canary -> full). we'll ask for staging access to mirror traffic for a short benchmark.
[10:38] Ethan: we can provide a traffic sample and a replay harness. we prefer a pilot start in calendar-december, with a goal to be in prod in q1. any blockers?
[10:48] Priya: timeline looks feasible but need k8s egress rules and private peering for VPC option. also SSO for access.

[12:30] Alex: cost deep-dive — the spike is partially explained by the fallback to fp variants and the long-context sessions, plus a small percentage of heavy batch jobs that ran without proper batching. we'll send a line-item CSV.
[12:46] Sofia: can you include per-route and per-model delta and suggested mitigations?
[12:51] Alex: yes — we'll include: per-route token counts, model variant cost, suggested batch settings, and cache warm strategies.

[15:05] Ethan: one more infra question — network egress between our VPC and Dedicated service, what's the expected bandwidth and cost?
[15:12] Miguel: depends on model size and tokens; we'll estimate based on your QPS and seq length. for Private on-prem it's different; we can produce a bandwidth estimate doc.

[18:00] Laura: for exec summary we need 1) root cause of cost spike, 2) proposed pilot plan with timeline and expected savings, 3) security checklist and delta to compliance. can redwood commit to a one-page executive brief?
[18:14] Alex: yes we'll produce a two-page exec brief and a one-page slide for your execs.

[20:10] Priya: operational notes — suggested immediate mitigations: tighten client retry jitter, set a soft per-route token limit, enable prefix caching for critical routes, and run a quick staging benchmark with a quantized profile.

[22:30] Sofia: curious — any best-practices from other customers on prompt engineering to reduce token length? we heard some teams put instructions server-side and only pass compact messages.
[22:45] Priya: yep that's common — move static system prompts to server-side cache and only send variable user content. also aggressive truncation for older context. we'll share a short prompts guide.

[25:00] Alex: ok near the end let's recap next steps — i'll email the cost CSV, miguel will share security doc, priya will coordinate pilot bench and staging access, sofia will send top prompts and traffic sample.

[25:20] Sofia: thanks, i'll get the prompts today.
[25:25] Ethan: i'll arrange the replay harness and pod logs for the october window.

[26:00] Miguel: we'll also include recommended RBAC roles and a sample SAML metadata file.

[27:10] Alex: perfect. any final concerns?
[27:20] Ravi: just one — we want to ensure that audit logs include token-level metadata but not PII; how is redwood redaction handled?
[27:31] Miguel: audit logs store request/response metadata by default; for Hosted we redact user content by policy, for Dedicated/Private we can configure retention and redaction rules to meet your compliance. we'll document options.

[30:00] Alex: cool, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the pilot kickoff.

End of meeting.
